beats.say: Objective 1 develops the Automatic Pricing Formula the proposal asks for, called APM-Bio. This first step sets the diesel price, the price that biodiesel has to beat.
The big number, RM 4,004.93/t, is the diesel benchmark called MOPS, Mean of Platts Singapore, for April 2026.
Where does it come from? From the master workbook, sheet MONTHLY DATA, cell H201. It is a stored number, not an Excel formula.
The Python pipeline rounds it to two decimals and saves it in the snapshot file as mopsRmT. Both studios read that saved value.

And how was cell H201 made? From Brent crude at 117.29 US dollars a barrel and an exchange rate of 3.9784 ringgit per dollar, using the recipe in the data dictionary. It stays a simulated proxy until a licensed MOPS price is supplied.

card.head: How H201 was made
card.body: Recipe from DATA DICTIONARY B13. The April season term has no input cell of its own.

beats.say: You can move this slider to test another diesel price, from 1,500 to 6,000 ringgit per tonne. The new value flows into the gap, into Objective 4 and into Decision now. Restore snapshot puts it back.
Developer view: the snapshot writer copies the April row into the decision snapshot, and both studios read it from there.
This step is the biodiesel cost, called PME, palm methyl ester. First choose a cost mode: Snapshot cost, the default, or Build from ingredients.
In Snapshot mode the number, RM 4,650.94/t, is read from cell I201 of the master workbook, rounded to two decimals and saved as pmeRmT.
Switch to Build from ingredients, and the studio works the cost out live from three inputs: last month's CPO price, methanol and glycerol.
The fitted equation is 168.9537, plus 1.0540 times March CPO, plus 0.1117 times methanol, minus 0.0945 times glycerol. That gives RM 4,628.39/t.
Why do the two modes differ by RM 22.55/t? Only a tiny part, RM 0.1655/t, is rounding. The rest is because the equation predicts the simulated cost series. It does not copy it.

lines: export function fittedPme(coefficients, { cpoLag, methanol, glycerol }) {
const c = key => Number(coefficients.find(row => row.Variable === key)?.Coefficient);
return c('const') + c('cpo_lag1') * Number(cpoLag) + c('meoh_rm') * Number(methanol) + c('gly_rm') * Number(glycerol);

beats.say: Now the two prices meet. The viability gap, VG, is the diesel price minus the biodiesel cost. APM-Bio is the formula, and the viability gap is the number it gives. It is the one name used for this number everywhere in the studios.
RM 4,004.93/t minus RM 4,650.94/t equals −RM 646.01/t.
The sign is what matters. Above zero, blending saves money. Below zero, biodiesel costs more, and support may be needed. Today the gap is negative, so the badge says Support needed.
A cross-check. The master workbook already stores this month's gap in cell J201: -646.0141590366225. Snapshot mode matches it to two decimals.
If you chose Build from ingredients in the last step, the viability gap becomes −RM 623.46/t. The history in the workbook does not change.

scenes.title: To find the break-even CPO price

beats.say: This step asks a different question. Pick a Brent crude price. The studio opens at 100 US dollars a barrel.
The answer is the break-even CPO price: the highest palm oil price at which biodiesel still costs no more than diesel. At Brent 100 it is RM 3,157.0/t.
First, a straight line fitted to all 196 months turns Brent into a diesel price. At 100 dollars that is about RM 3,401.6/t.
Then it sets the biodiesel cost equation equal to that diesel price, and solves for CPO. Methanol and glycerol stay at their April values.
Finally it compares with the real April CPO price, RM 4,567.5/t. CPO is RM 1,410.5/t above break-even, so at this oil price biodiesel cannot beat diesel.
Keep two numbers apart. RM 4,628.39/t is a biodiesel cost. RM 3,157.0/t is a CPO threshold. And at Brent 60 the threshold falls to RM 1,894.4/t.

scenes.title: To test the long-run price link

beats.say: Developer level only. This step tests whether three prices move together over the long run, using the Johansen trace test.
It uses real public data: the biodiesel export unit value, the local CPO price, and Brent in ringgit. 172 months, from 2012-01 to 2026-04, in natural logs.
For each lag setting, one to eight, it computes a trace statistic. When the bar is taller than the 5 percent critical value, 29.80, the test rejects no link.
All 8 of 8 lag settings reject rank zero. This counts lag settings, not separate relationships.
Read this before reporting hypothesis H1. The test uses export value, CPO and Brent. The proposal's H1 names a different set of prices, so this result does not confirm that set.

card.head: Read before reporting H1
card.body: This test: export value · CPO · Brent (MYR). Proposal H1: PME · MOPS Diesel · Brent. Cost equation: PME · CPO(t−1) · methanol · glycerol. One result does not confirm the other two.

beats.say: Developer view: the trace statistic is minus T times the sum of the log of one minus each eigenvalue, in the cointegration script.

scenes.title: To see how the fund moves each month

beats.say: Objective 3 asks whether a Biodiesel Stabilisation Fund can withstand oil price fluctuations, with the money from Objective 2. The fund is one running balance: the opening balance, plus money in, minus support paid, gives the closing balance.

The opening balance starts at RM 1,000 mn. This is not data, because the fund does not exist yet. It is the proposed starting money from Objective 2, set in v3 config and saved in the snapshot as seedCapitalRmMn.

Money in is the sources from Objective 2. Each month the fund receives one twelfth of each yearly source, plus any savings that month. Support goes out when biodiesel costs more than diesel. What is left is the closing balance, and it opens the next month.

card.head: The monthly rule
card.work:
F(t) = max(0, F(t−1) + savings + income − support)
income  = (export-point levy + production tax + BSL) ÷ 12
savings = max(VG, 0) × monthly B20 tonnes × share
support = max(−VG, 0) × monthly B20 tonnes

beats.say: The income comes from the last 12 rows of the master workbook, May 2025 to April 2026. Column K, CPO production, adds up to 20,647.26 thousand tonnes, and column L, palm oil exports, to 16,318.03 thousand tonnes.

The export-point levy is 25 ringgit on 16.318 million tonnes, and the production tax and the BSL are 25 ringgit each on 20.647 million tonnes. Together that is RM 1,440.31 mn a year, or RM 120.03 mn a month.

beats.say: Support is paid on the B20 blend, and its size comes from diesel use. Column Q, over the same 12 months, averages 878.38 million litres a month.
878.38 million litres a month, times 12 months, times the 20 percent blend, times 0.88 tonnes per thousand litres, is 1.8551 million tonnes a year. Divided by 12, that is 154,595 tonnes a month.
An example with the April viability gap. Opening fund RM 1,000 mn. Income in: RM 120.03 mn. Support out: 646.01 ringgit times 154,595 tonnes, which is RM 99.87 mn. The month closes at RM 1,020.16 mn.

beats.say: Why 90 percent? It comes from hypothesis H2 in the accepted proposal: the fund must sustain deficits for at least 6 months under the 90th percentile Monte Carlo shock. Surviving every shock up to the 90th percentile means lasting in at least 90 percent of the paths. It is the confidence level the proposal chose, not a number calculated from data, and it sits in the studio code, not in the workbook. 100.0% is above it, so it meets the target.

The proposal gives no formula for 85%; it is a policy choice in the research design, kept in v3 config as the solvency target. 9.2% is far below it.

scenes.title: To apply the B20 / B30 rule

beats.say: Here the three checks meet. The viability gap fails, the fund passes, and approval is off.
Card 1 repeats the viability gap from step 1: −RM 646.01/t, below zero, so it fails.
Card 2 says above RM 693 mn. That is the RM 693.48 mn limit from step 2, rounded to a whole million. The fund, 1,000 million, is above it, so it passes.
Card 3 is the approval switch from step 3. It is off, and only the government can turn it on.
Notice what is not here: the Objective 3 survival answer. That test ran the fund on B20, and this rule does not read it.
The rule runs in order. B30 only if all three pass. B15 only if the gap is below minus 500 and the fund is not safe. Otherwise, B20.

beats.say: Developer level only. Pick an energy level, a geopolitical run and the highest blend allowed. The studio shows one saved 5 year result out of 18: 3 energy levels, times 3 geopolitical runs, times 2 ceilings, each on 2,000 price paths.

Energy levels set where Brent drifts: Low 80, Baseline 105 and High 135 dollars. The Russia level shift raises that target by 25 percent for good. The Middle East spike adds a 40 percent jump that fades over about five months. Each path starts with the 1,000 million fund and the same money coming in as the fund test, and uses the fund limit from step 2.
Mean cost over 5 years. For each of the 2,000 paths, the support paid in all 60 months is added up. Then the 2,000 totals are averaged: RM 9,028.2 mn, shown as RM 9,028 mn.

card.head: How each 5-year measure is made · one saved run
card.work:
cost of a path  = Σ support over 60 months
mean cost      = average of the 2,000 path costs
P95 cost       = 95th percentile of the path costs
cost σ         = standard deviation of the path costs
median fund    = the middle path's balance after month 60
CPO absorbed   = blend tonnes over 60 months, path average
switches/year  = blend changes on a path ÷ 5, path average
Brent mean     = average Brent over all months and paths

beats.say: P95 cost: 95 percent of the paths cost less than RM 15,925 mn. It is the bad-case cost.
Cost sigma, RM 4,160.6 mn, is the standard deviation of those 2,000 path costs: how widely they spread.
Median final fund: put the 2,000 balances after month 60 in order, and take the middle one. It is RM 0 mn, so the fund is empty at the end in at least half of the paths.

CPO absorbed: the biodiesel tonnes used over the 5 years, averaged over paths, 8.42 million tonnes. That is less than 5 years of B20, 9.28 million, because the rule drops to B15 in months when the fund is not safe.
Switches per year: how often the blend changes on a path, averaged over the paths and divided by 5 years: 0.63.
Brent mean: the average Brent price over all months of all paths, 111 dollars. It is above the 105 target because every path starts at April's 117.29 dollars and drifts down slowly.
In the default run, allowing B30 gives a mean 5 year cost of RM 9,028 mn, against RM 9,028 mn for B20 only.

Look at the P95 row, the bad-case cost. It matches between the two ceilings. B30 only runs when the viability gap is positive, when no support is paid, so it adds palm oil use without adding worst-case cost.

card.head: How to read it
card.body: Energy: Low USD 80, Baseline 105, High 135. Runs: Normal, Russia level shift (+25% lasting), Middle East spike (+40% that fades). Named runs, not a probability scale.

scenes.title: To compare cost swings with fixed blends

beats.say: Hypothesis H4 says the rule should cut monthly cost swings by at least 25 percent. The three bars compare fixed B20, fixed B30 and the rule.

The back-test runs the rule on all 196 months from January 2010 to April 2026, starting with a fund of 1,000 million and the same money as the fund test, with B30 approval assumed. Each month's cost is the support paid that month.
The rule's swing, RM 116.9 mn, is the standard deviation of those 196 monthly costs. They average RM 134.7 mn a month.

card.head: The rule's swing
card.work:
monthly cost = support paid that month, 2010-01 to 2026-04
standard deviation of 196 costs = RM 116.9195 mn
average = RM 134.7128 mn a month

beats.say: Fixed B20 shows the same RM 116.9 mn, because in the pipeline the fixed B20 series is the rule's own cost series, times 20 divided by 20.
Fixed B30 is the same series times 30 divided by 20, so its swing is one and a half times larger: 116.92 times 1.5 is 175.38.
So against fixed B30 the swing is 1 minus 116.92 divided by 175.38: 33.3% smaller, which meets the 25 percent target. Because of the scaling, it is exactly one third.

beats.say: Against fixed B20 it is 1 minus 116.92 divided by 116.92: 0.0%, below the target, and zero by the same scaling.

card.title: vs fixed B20 · cut = 1 − rule ÷ B20

scenes.title: To see what moving to B30 would change

beats.say: What would moving to B30 change? The four effects use the master's last 12 months, May 2025 to April 2026. First, the gap: column J averages minus 1,845.60 ringgit per tonne over those months.
Extra government support: the average shortfall, 1,845.60 ringgit per tonne, times the extra tonnes of B30 over B20, 2.7827 minus 1.8551 million. About RM 1,712 mn a year.
Next, diesel use. Column Q averages 878.38 million litres a month over the same 12 months. It sets the size of every blend.
Second, extra CPO used at home: the extra 10 percent of blend on that diesel. 878.38 times 12 times 10 percent times 0.88 is 0.928 million tonnes a year, shown as 0.93.
Third, fossil diesel replaced: the same 878.38 million litres a month, times 12, times the extra 10 percent of blend, is 1.054 billion litres a year.
Fourth, biodiesel production. Column M adds up to 1,630.8 thousand tonnes over the same 12 months, which is 1.6308 million tonnes.
PME needed compared with recent output: the B30 tonnes, 2.7827 million, divided by 1.6308 million, is 1.71 times. Above 1 means current output is short.
Carbon dioxide avoided is not estimated until an approved lifecycle emission factor is supplied.

card.head: Not estimated yet
card.body: CO₂ avoided needs an approved lifecycle emission factor. Diesel use and PME output are legacy inputs; replace them with approved series before official use.

The limit is the same: 3 times the back-test's recent average support of RM 231.16 mn, which is RM 693.48 mn. 1,000 is more than 693.48, so it passes.
Money coming in opens a small calculator. It has its own BSL rate and savings share, starting from the Objective 2 values: 25 ringgit per tonne and 100 percent.
With both fixed sources, the money in each year is RM 408 mn plus RM 516 mn plus RM 516 mn plus RM 81 mn: RM 1,521.0 mn, the same sum as Objective 2. It does not change the blend.
